weeks.weekly_summary: RECOVERY WEEK: reduce volume to ~35 km (−24% from Week 3). Maintain one quality session (tempo 5km) and keep long run structured (12km, −20% from Week 3). Focus on restoration and consolidating Week 1–3 adaptations.
weeks.coaching_notes: Week 4 is the mandated recovery week to consolidate 3 weeks of progressive stress. Volume drops significantly; long run trims to 12km (−3km from Week 3). One quality session (tempo 5km) is retained to maintain threshold fitness without excessive fatigue. Total time ~4:00 hrs, well below the 7-hour budget. This week allows adaptation, injury prevention, and nervous system recovery. Use extra time for mobility, sleep, and mental preparation. Plan to return stronger in the next block.

coaching_overview: This 4-week Base Building block establishes aerobic foundation and introduces quality sessions (tempo runs, fartlek, and long runs) to build lactate threshold and endurance. Week 1 anchors at 40km with two quality sessions (6km tempo + 11km long run). Week 2 progresses to 44km, extending tempo to 7km and long run to 13km. Week 3 peaks at 46km, introducing fartlek work (6 × 2min hard) on Thursday while maintaining a 15km long run on Sunday. Week 4 recovers with reduced volume (35km), lightened tempo (5km), and shortened long run (12km). All paces are derived from current Strava fitness (easy: 6:43/km; tempo: 5:55/km). Training follows polarized principles (75–82% easy, 18–25% hard) and respects the 7-hour weekly time budget. No race date is set; the athlete should define a target marathon date and race time to enable pace targeting and taper planning in subsequent blocks. Progression is conservative, respecting the 10% rule and ensuring no consecutive hard days. Week 4 allows full restoration before entering the Aerobic Development phase (Weeks 5+) with longer tempos, marathon-pace segments, and extended long runs.
